Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
articles.abstract: Abstract How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

articles.title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
articles.abstract: Abstract Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

articles.title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
articles.abstract: Abstract Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

articles.title: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage
A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
articles.abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans . Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans , chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

articles.title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
articles.abstract: Abstract Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

articles.title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
articles.abstract: Abstract Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

articles.title:
Reductive Incorporation
of Technetium-99 in Fe(II)-Doped
Layered Double Hydroxide
articles.abstract: Abstract Technetium-99 is a long-lived, high-yield fission product whose solubility is controlled by redox conditions. Here, to explore targeted effluent treatment approaches, pertechnetate (Tc(VII)O4–) reductive retention as Tc(IV) during coprecipitation of Fe(II)-doped Ni–Al–CO3 layered double hydroxide (LDH) was investigated. During LDH formation via base addition to an acidic Ni2+, Al3+, Fe2+, and Tc(VII)O4– bearing solution, there was essentially complete TcO4– removal at low (9.6 Bq/mL) and high (2.9 kBq/mL) concentrations. Characterization of experiments using X-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirmed that, during base titration, a two-stage process occurred, with Al3+ forming amorphous Al (hydr)oxide between pH 4 and 6 in the first stage, followed by hydrolysis of Fe2+/Ni2+ and formation of LDH particles between pH 6 and 9 in stage two. During the first stage, TcO4– was removed from solution, and XAS confirmed it was reduced to Tc(IV) by Fe(II) associated with the amorphous Al (hydr)oxide, forming hydrous Tc(IV)O2-like chains on the Al (hydr)oxide surface. During the second stage, XAS showed that Tc(IV) was incorporated within the newly formed LDH structure. Overall, these data provide novel insights into the application of LDH formation in Tc sequestration and suggest novel effluent treatment pathways to produce an inorganic solid.

articles.title:
Modeled
Groundwater Decline is Associated with Lower
Arsenic Concentrations in Hanoi
articles.abstract: Abstract Elevated arsenic concentrations in groundwater pose health risks. Geogenic arsenic contamination is driven by biogeochemical mobilization and groundwater dynamics. Intensive pumping can initially exacerbate contamination by drawing arsenic or mobilizing organic matter into aquifers, but over longer time scales may also promote dilution and flushing in some settings. To better understand the mechanisms controlling arsenic concentrations, we examined changes over two decades in Hanoi (Vietnam), a hotspot of geogenic arsenic contamination and groundwater pumping. Arsenic concentrations from 470 wells sampled in the year 2000 were compared with 434 wells sampled in the same area in 2013 and 2023. Median concentrations declined from 14 to 8 μg/L between 2000 and 2023, while mean concentrations and the proportion of high-arsenic wells (>100 μg/L) remained similar. Using hydrochemical and groundwater-level data, CatBoost models combined with SHAP analysis assessed changes in predictor importance. In 2000, arsenic was more strongly associated with redox predictors, whereas groundwater-level predictors became more important in 2023. Within wells used to evaluate groundwater-level change (n = 251), larger decadal declines were associated with lower arsenic concentrations (median = 31 μg/L) than wells without declines (median = 120 μg/L). We hypothesize a decadal mechanism shift, from redox to hydrological controls, particularly driving arsenic declines.

articles.title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl − ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl − contact ion pairs that make Cl − migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co–Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH * and OOH * during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm −2 ) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm −2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm −2 ) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.

articles.title: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
articles.abstract: Abstract Flow diverter (FD) implantation is standard for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), but cerebrovascular complications persist. This nested study within a prospective multicenter cohort evaluates whether short-term, low-dose glucocorticoid use is associated with cerebrovascular outcomes after FD implantation. Propensity-score matching with exact matching on UIA location yielded 1327 patients (360 glucocorticoid-treated; 967 controls). Intravenous glucocorticoids, initiated within 2 hours of the FD procedure and administered for ≥2 days, were associated with fewer in-hospital cerebrovascular events (6.9% vs. 13.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.53) and major cerebrovascular events (4.7% vs. 12.4%; aOR, 0.37). Over a median 2-year follow-up, glucocorticoid use was also associated with fewer new-onset major cerebrovascular events (3.6% vs. 8.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.41) and less in-stent stenosis (7.9% vs. 13.2%; aOR, 0.55). Findings remained robust in unmatched patients on sensitivity analyses. We demonstrate that perioperative glucocorticoid regimens may reduce cerebrovascular events and in-stent stenosis in FD-treated patients, warranting randomized trials.

articles.title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation

Rationally micropatterned antifogging hydrogels counteracting extreme condensation
articles.abstract: Abstract Loss of transparency due to water vapor condensation is a widespread problem across diverse applications such as windows, eyewear, displays, vehicles, and kitchenware. Conventional antifogging strategies relying on hydrophilic or hydrophobic coatings, based on chemistry and/or nano-topography, can counteract up to mild water deposition, but lose functionality at excessive condensation environments. Here, we present a passive approach, rationally micropatterning an inherently hydrophilic hydrogel to maintain high transparency under supersaturation. Guided by optics and wetting theory, and employing a diffusion model to calculate related timescales of water film formation, we engineer a wicking structure on poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate hydrogel, facilitating long-term sustainable filmwise condensation. Employing quantitative optical clarity measurements and visualization, we show that our approach clearly outperforms state-of-the-art antifogging alternatives, retaining high optical clarity even in boiling environments. Facile fabrication and superior performance establish our microstructured hydrogel as an excellent choice for sustaining transparency under extreme condensation.

articles.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB
articles.abstract: Abstract WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31–56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11–0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07–0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features—particularly in-combination—identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

articles.title:
Life-Cycle Burden
Shifting in Solvent-Based Regeneration
of PFOS-Laden Granular Activated Carbon
articles.abstract: Abstract Granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely used to remove perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) from contaminated water, yet its sustainable regeneration remains challenging. Solvent-based regeneration preserves the carbon matrix but may shift environmental burdens toward solvent production, chemical use, energy demand, and downstream waste management. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) of PFOS-laden GAC regeneration using deionized water (GAC-WR) and ethanol (GAC-ER). We identify electricity-driven elution and downstream incineration as the dominant environmental hotspots across 18 midpoint impact categories. Selected chemical-assisted configurations (NaOH-modified water and HCl-modified ethanol) improved regeneration efficiency and reduced environmental impacts under the evaluated conditions by reducing virgin GAC supplementation. An industrial-scale model incorporating equipment upscaling and thermal integration further mitigated laboratory-specific energy overestimation. Compared with the corresponding baseline scenarios using the global electricity mix, hydropower-based electricity reduces global warming potential to 3.30 and 8.26 kg CO2e kg–1 for GAC-WR and GAC-ER, respectively, while increasing life-cycle water consumption to 230% and 266% of the respective baselines. This cross-category burden shift demonstrates that reducing climate impacts does not necessarily reduce the broader life-cycle environmental footprint. Overall, sustainable solvent-based GAC regeneration requires balancing regeneration efficiency, energy supply, chemical inputs, solvent recovery, and management of PFAS-containing wastes.

articles.title:
Micromolar Experiments,
Nanomolar Environments

Nanoplastic Size
Governs the Decoupling of Microbial
Survival from Antibiotic Degradation
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L–1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.

articles.title:
Early
Life Ambient
Air Pollution, Sex Steroids and
Neurodevelopment: Target Trial Emulation in a Prospective Cohort
articles.abstract: Abstract Ambient air pollution may impair childhood neurodevelopment, but sensitive windows, mediating pathways, and the neurodevelopmental benefits of air-quality interventions remain unclear. In this prospective birth cohort of 3575 mother–child pairs in Wuhan, China (2014–2019), neurodevelopment at age two was assessed using the Bayley Scales, and cord serum sex steroids were measured in 897 pairs. Associations of air pollution exposure from preconception through the second postnatal year with neurodevelopment at age two and potential sex-steroid mediation were evaluated. Target trial emulation (TTE) was used to estimate neurodevelopmental differences associated with China’s 2013–2017 air-quality intervention. Most air pollutants were inversely associated with neurodevelopment across multiple exposure windows, with associations generally strongest during the first postnatal year. Mediation analyses suggested that androstenedione mediated 5–12% of associations between specific preconception/prenatal air pollutant exposures and Psychomotor Development Index, although inverse-probability-weighted indirect effects were no longer statistically significant. TTE suggested significant neurodevelopmental benefits following the air-quality intervention, with Mental Development Index and Psychomotor Development Index improving by 7.27 and 6.41 points in the later policy-period group, respectively. These findings support more stringent long-term air pollution standards and sustained air-quality interventions to protect child neurodevelopment.

articles.title:
Gas–Liquid
Interface Enhanced Selective Adsorption
of Long-Chain PFAS by Novel Floating Macroporous Resins
articles.abstract: Abstract Long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in industrial wastewater are a significant source of PFAS contamination. Anion exchange resin (AER) adsorption is an advantageous technology for PFAS removal, but existing AERs suffer from limited selectivity. In this study, our synthesized novel macroporous AERs with asymmetric long-chain amine groups, MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1), exhibited a unique floating behavior on the water surface after drying and achieved significantly enhanced PFAS removal from chromium-plating wastewater, with the gas–liquid interface playing a critical role. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the rough surfaces and hydrophobic functional groups of the dry MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1) enable them to maintain the Cassie wetting state in water without transitioning to the Wenzel state, thereby forming a stable gas–liquid interface. The gas–liquid interface exhibited adsorption free energies reaching −7.6 to −9.5 kcal/mol for long-chain PFAS, increasing the selectivity of the floating macroporous AERs for various long-chain PFAS by 6–81 times. This provides a new approach for the efficient removal of long-chain PFAS and offers new insights for the design of selective adsorbents based on the gas–liquid interface.

articles.title:
Submicroscale
and
Molecular Insights into Labile Organic
Matter Transformation and Sequestration at Newly Formed Iron Minerals–Water
Interfaces during O2-Mediated Fe(II) Oxidation
articles.abstract: Abstract Abiotic Fe(II) oxidation and subsequent precipitation are key pathways for controlling labile organic matter (OM) dynamics in O2-perturbed subsurface environments, yet the underlying coupling mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, OM transformation and sequestration during O2-mediated heterogeneous Fe(II) oxidation were evaluated at neutral pH across various C/Fe ratios. Increasing C/Fe ratios impeded Fe(II) oxidation but enhanced the level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Despite efficient sequestration, the OM immobilization efficiency varied with C/Fe ratios, with a minor fraction of OM being oxidized by ROS. Higher C/Fe ratios promoted ferrihydrite formation but inhibited its transformation into lepidocrocite, forming mineral-organic composites constituted by Fe–O cores and edge-/corner-sharing Fe–Fe shells. A direct visualization at submicroscale revealed heterogeneous spatial distributions of different organo functional groups on newly formed Fe mineral surfaces, reflecting OM selective immobilization. Newly formed Fe minerals preferentially immobilized high-molecular-weight compounds and those with more oxygenated or highly unsaturated structures, with stronger molecular fractionation at higher C/Fe ratios. Molecular-level analysis revealed that a lower C/Fe ratio promoted the conversion of phenols to quinones, aromatic ring opening, and carboxylation of aromatic substituents but inhibited polymerization of phenolic substances. Collectively, these findings deepen our knowledge of heterogeneous Fe mineral formation coupled with OM sequestration and transformation, advancing our understanding of Fe and C geochemical cycling in oxic soils and sediments.

articles.title: Ocean Acidification Impairs Olfaction in the Large Yellow Croaker, Larimichthys crocea , by Disrupting Sensory Integrity and Neural Processing
articles.abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification (OA) poses a significant threat to marine organisms, yet its effects on fish sensory systems remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of elevated pCO2 on olfactory function in the large yellow croaker, Larimichthys crocea. Elevated pCO2 reduced peripheral olfactory sensitivity, as evidenced by suppressed electro-olfactogram responses. This impairment was accompanied by epithelial disorganization, cellular damage, increased apoptosis in the olfactory epithelium, and reduced expression of olfactory neuron markers. In vitro analyses using a selected recombinant L. crocea odorant receptor LORA1–1 showed that acidified pH altered its physicochemical properties and odorant-specific receptor–ligand interaction dynamics. OA also downregulated genes associated with odorant receptor expression, G protein-mediated signaling, calcium-related transduction, and neuronal maturation. Telencephalic responses included altered ion-transport ATPase activities, histopathological abnormalities, oxidative stress, enhanced apoptotic activity, and reduced neuropeptide Y expression. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identified telencephalic molecular changes associated with altered neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, calcium signaling, glutathione metabolism, apoptosis, mitophagy, MAPK signaling, and olfactory transduction. Our findings suggest that epithelial injury, altered odorant recognition, and disrupted peripheral signaling contribute to OA-induced olfactory impairment in L. crocea, with potential consequences for migration and reproduction that depend on olfactory cues.

articles.title:
Uncovering
the Fate
and Global-Scale Risk-Based Threshold
Contents of Organophosphate Esters in Indoor Environments: A Tiered
Modeling Approach
articles.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous indoors, posing threats to public health. However, limited information on both the permissible levels and environmental behavior makes global regulation challenging. Herein, a closed-loop mechanistic framework, termed the Indoor OPE Source Identification and Exposure Direct Assessment (IOSIEDA) model, tracing the cause-and-effect chain from OPE source contents to health impacts, was developed to forecast indoor OPE emissions and fate, rapidly screen risks, prioritize high-risk OPE-material combinations, and back-calculate risk-based threshold contents (RTCs). Model evaluation via Monte Carlo simulation and a residential case study revealed a total Σ13OPEs influx of ∼2053 μg day–1, predominantly originating from indoor source emissions (99.4%), with 95% loss via air exchange. Notably, the IOSIEDA model back-calculated the RTCs within a risk-based framework built upon the source-specific relationship between OPE contents and emission characteristics, developing health-prevention-oriented thresholds for a set of unregulated OPEs across five types of understudied source materials. Global application across 16 countries provided emissions and an RTC database for indoor OPEs, filling in the missing values for global national thresholds of OPEs in specific source materials. Total residential OPE emissions were estimated at ∼74,500 kg yr–1; Asia constitutes the major emission region, and RTCs exhibit distinct regional disparities across continents.

articles.title: Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
articles.abstract: Abstract Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.

articles.title:
Voltage-Dependent
Metabolic Shifts Regulate the Fouling
Behavior of the Anaerobic-Anodic Membrane
articles.abstract: Abstract Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical–microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.

articles.title:
Halogenated Nucleosides:
Highly Toxic Biogenic Disinfection
Byproducts Prevalent in Drinking Water
articles.abstract: Abstract Five decades of research on disinfection byproducts (DBPs) reveals only the tip of the iceberg, with humus as their primary precursor. Here, we identified 15 halogenated nucleosides (HNSs) as new DBPs originating from biological materials in drinking water. A nationwide survey across China revealed that their individual detection frequencies ranged from 87% to 100%, with the maximum concentration reaching 141 ng/L. Two quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models were developed based on the cytotoxicity and genotoxicity data, with dipole moment (μ) and sum of the degree of valence (SVDe) as key cytotoxicity descriptors, and molar refractivity (R) together with number of H-bond donors (NHD) for genotoxicity. Integrated concentration and toxicity data revealed that halogenated (deoxy)cytidines and halogenated (deoxy)adenosines warrant priority regulatory consideration. The concentrations of HNSs were positively correlated with both pH (r = 0.6, P = 0.0005) and residual chlorine (r = 0.5, P = 0.0095) of drinking water samples, which may be related to local precipitation, temperature, and economic development. This study expands the scope of DBP research beyond humus-derived DBPs to biomolecule-derived ones.

articles.title:
Perspectives and
Mitigation Methods for Underappreciated
Amine Escape from CO2 Desorption
articles.abstract: Abstract Amine-based CO2 capture is increasingly limited by amine escape and aerosol emissions that drive solvent loss and secondary pollution. Research has focused on the absorber, leaving the desorption section─where intensive CO2 release, water-vapor entrainment, and rapid cooling coincide─overlooked as an escape source. Here, we combine molecular dynamics simulations with bench-scale experiments to resolve the mechanism and control of amine escape during CO2 desorption. Counter to absorber-side expectations, a CO2-rich atmosphere suppresses rather than promotes aerosol nucleation: elevated CO2 competitively disrupts the H2O–H2O hydrogen-bond network stabilizing water-centered nuclei, with stable clusters essentially absent at 75 vol % CO2. New aerosol formation is thus favored near the low-CO2 reboiler outlet, while cooling in the upper column grows preexisting aerosols. Measurements revealed an 82% decrease in the total amine concentration along the column, consistent with the descending rich solvent acting as an important amine sink, while preexisting aerosols continued to grow in the upper section. Guided by this mechanism, a combined mitigation strategy is proposed: a low-volatility solvent formulation lowered aerosol by 66% relative to MEA, increasing the rich-solvent CO2 loading offered a favorable trade-off, and upstream scrubbing–condensation captured residual species. Together, these measures reduced amine escape by over 99% (to <1.4 ppm) while increasing CO2 product purity. By reframing the desorber as a key emission unit, these results support strategies for reducing desorber-side amine and aerosol emissions.

articles.title:
Bromine Monoxide
Radical Likely Dominates Dimethylsulfide
Oxidation before the Springtime Onset of Arctic Ice Melt
articles.abstract: Abstract To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethylsulfone (DMSO2), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS accompany depleted O3, high surface albedo, and air temperatures < 0 °C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions, suggesting that BrO•-initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. In GEOS-Chem simulations, BrO• is the dominant oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO• concentrations from sea-salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O3, DMSO, and DMSO2, suggesting a missing source of reactive bromine from sunlit saline snow. BrO•-initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to •OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, •OH oxidation likely dominates Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as the sea-ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.

articles.title:
Evaluating Community-Level
Effects of 6PPD-Quinone
in a Natural Boreal Lake Ecosystem
articles.abstract: Abstract 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire rubber antioxidant 6PPD, is an emerging contaminant known for its acute toxicity to certain salmonids. However, its potential impacts on aquatic communities remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, 6PPD-Q-spiked limnocorrals were deployed in a natural boreal lake, and water chemistry, phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate communities were assessed over 28 days following a single pulse exposure (0–100 μg/L) simulating stormwater runoff. Waterborne 6PPD-Q concentrations declined by 80–99% by the end of the study, with no detectable effects on water chemistry or aquatic communities. Temporal changes in chlorophyll-a concentrations and zooplankton abundance were attributed to seasonal dynamics rather than 6PPD-Q exposure, and benthic invertebrate community composition remained unchanged. Concurrently, wild-spawned fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas) embryos were exposed to 6PPD-Q-spiked water collected from the limnocorrals. Larval survival declined significantly at 100 μg/L, with altered hatch timing and sublethal effects including reduced growth, changes in eye, yolk sac, and pericardial areas, and altered energy allocation. These effects occurred at 10.6–22.4 μg/L and above, concentrations that exceed those so far reported in surface waters and stormwater by approximately an order of magnitude. Collectively, this study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q effects on aquatic communities and early life-stage fish. Environmental Significance. This study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q impacts on freshwater communities. While broad aquatic communities appeared resilient to short-term exposure scenarios, early life stages of fish responded at concentrations above those currently reported in the environment, identifying developmental end points that warrant attention when assessing the risks of tire-derived contaminants in freshwater ecosystems.

articles.title:
Atmospheric
Removal
of Nitrous Oxide: Approaches and
Feasibility
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third-largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing and the dominant anthropogenic ozone-depleting emission. While mitigation can flatten emissions, there is no clear pathway to eliminate residual emissions from agriculture and other diffuse sources, a key challenge for climate stabilization. The potential role of atmospheric removal has not been holistically assessed, yet N2O’s high potency and long atmospheric lifetime indicate the potential for a durable climate benefit. This review synthesizes emerging approaches for atmospheric N2O removal, organized by reaction mechanism (thermal destruction and thermocatalysis, photolysis, gas-phase radical reactions, photocatalysis, and biological reduction) and deployment format (closed versus open system). Each is evaluated for technical efficacy, climate viability, environmental and social viability, and economic plausibility using lower-bound cost models. No approach yet satisfies all four: gas-phase radical reactors are precluded by their kinetics, thermocatalytic and photocatalytic reactors require ten- to hundred-fold performance gains, and open-system approaches have the lowest cost floors but face the greatest measurement and governance challenges. These results identify the performance thresholds and broader constraints that govern feasibility across pathways, providing a foundation for a research agenda and for assessing the role of N2O removal alongside emissions mitigation.

articles.title:
Toward Rational
Design of Low-Salt-Rejection Reverse
Osmosis for Minimal and Zero Liquid Discharge
articles.abstract: Abstract Low-salt-rejection reverse osmosis (LSRRO) has emerged as a promising technology for concentrating high-salinity brines in minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge (MLD/ZLD) applications. However, rational LSRRO design remains hindered by uncertainties about how existing modeling frameworks should be interpreted and applied. In this Perspective, we critically examine the limitations of process modeling and module-scale analysis in LSRRO design. Conventional process models can yield misleading predictions for spiral-wound LSRRO modules because the stagewise concentration cutoff embedded in these models is based on the cumulative permeate composition rather than the local permeate conditions that govern water transport. Experimental results and local transport calculations show that the brine concentration in spiral-wound LSRRO stages is not constrained by a fixed thermodynamic concentration cutoff. Nevertheless, standalone process models remain inherently limited in assessing practical feasibility because they do not resolve kinetic constraints, such as declining water flux along the module. Module-scale analysis is therefore essential for linking local transport behavior to practical design metrics, including membrane area requirements, productivity, and achievable brine concentration. However, its predictive accuracy is constrained because transport parameters derived from conventional local transport models vary with salinity, which challenges their use as constants across the module. This Perspective therefore highlights the need for condition-dependent and experimentally validated local transport descriptions to enable rational LSRRO design for future MLD/ZLD applications.

articles.title:
Selective
Oxidation
of Sulfoxide to Sulfone in Chloride/Peroxymonosulfate
Systems: Reassessing a Diagnostic Probe for High-Valent Metal-Oxo
Identification
articles.abstract: Abstract The selective oxidation of sulfoxides to sulfones, particularly using methyl phenyl sulfoxide (PMSO), has been widely adopted for over a decade as a diagnostic method for high-valent metal-oxo (HVMO) species in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). Here, we demonstrate that this transformation proceeds efficiently via non-HVMO pathways in metal-free systems, challenging the probe’s specificity. Using the chloride/peroxymonosulfate (Cl−/PMS) system as a model, PMSO is converted to methyl phenyl sulfone (PMSO2) with high selectivity (83.5%−98.7%) across pH 3.5−11. Kinetic, isotopic, and computational analyses reveal a pH-dependent mechanistic switch for the high-yield transformation of PMSO to PMSO2. Under acidic conditions, Cl2/HOCl generated from the two-electron oxidation of Cl− by HSO5− through nucleophilic addition mediate oxygen-atom transfer from water via a chlorosulfonium cation intermediate, with Cl2 dominating PMSO selective oxidation (kapp = 1.58 × 106 M−1 s−1; 47.91 M−1 s−1 for HOCl). Under alkaline conditions, nucleophilic attack by SO52− formed via PMS hydrolysis becomes predominant (16.38 M−1 s−1). The reaction kinetics are linearly dependent on Cl− concentration, and similar selective oxidation is observed in other metal-free AOPs (e.g., base/PMS, HCO3−/PMS, and Cl−/peracetic acid). Our findings necessitate reassessing the sulfoxide probe’s specificity for HVMO identification in PMS-based systems containing chloride or alkalinity, and underscore the imperative for rigorous mechanistic validation in water treatment.

articles.title:
Sex-Specific
Associations of Gestational OPE Exposure
with Offspring Digit Ratio: A Birth Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Abstract The effect of prenatal organophosphate esters (OPEs) exposure on offspring reproductive development and the potential role of the placenta remain unclear. We investigated the associations of prenatal OPE exposure with the second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) and the mediating role of placental DNA methylation (DNAm) levels of PPAR pathway genes. Maternal urine OPE metabolites at 12–16 gestational weeks were measured. Placental DNAm levels at birth and children’s 2D:4D at ages 4 and 6 years were assessed. Multiple linear regression, BKMR, and causal mediation analyses were applied. We observed associations between prenatal exposure to BBOEP, BEHP, DBP, and DPP and increased 2D:4D in boys, whereas DBP and DCP were associated with decreased 2D:4D in girls. BKMR identified alkyl-OPEs, particularly BBOEP, as the primary contributors in boys. Moreover, hypermethylation of RXRA, ACAA1, and ACADM was associated with decreased 2D:4D in all populations. In girls, the associations among higher OPE exposure, increased ACAA1 methylation, and lower 2D:4D suggested a potential mediation pathway, while the mediation effects were not statistically significant. These findings suggest sex-specific associations between prenatal OPE exposure and 2D:4D. The potential role of placental PPAR-related DNAm in these associations warrants further investigation.
